Alex: heads up — after landing adaptive-kernel routing change in canary, we see a microbatch sizing regression when streaming chat is enabled. p95/p99 jump for small-reqs. digging in.
Priya: can you paste the perf numbers? streaming vs non-streaming? :thinking:
Alex: short summary: with mb_size=1 -> streaming chat p95 ~85ms p99 ~310ms; mb_size=4 -> streaming p95 ~120ms p99 ~520ms. For non-streaming completions (sync bulk) mb_size=4 gives much better throughput and lower p99 (p99 down ~30%). So tradeoff obvious but numbers worse than expected.
Mateo: interesting. do we get different kernel selection for streaming path? maybe fallback to slower attention kernels when mb>1?
Alex: yes — profiler shows kernel picker takes path: for seq_len<=128 & single-token streaming we use fast-causal-kernel-v2. When microbatch groups requests, the kernel selector switches to grouped-attn-kernel (less optimized for tiny tails). Logged: `kernel: fast-causal-kernel-v2 -> grouped-attn-kernel` when mb>1.
Jordan: are KV cache hits changing? grouping could change KV alignment, causing more cache spills.
Alex: KV stats from canary (10k requests): mb=1 streaming: kv_hit=92.1% kv_spill=0.6%; mb=4 streaming: kv_hit=87.3% kv_spill=1.9%. Miss delta small but correlates with p99 tail in traces — more tailwork due to KV fetch/merge overhead.
Sam: can we force kernel for streaming to fast-causal-kernel-v2 even when mb>1 as a test? maybe it's safe perf-wise though less optimized for throughput.
Priya: yes try an override config and run A/B for 2h window, check p50/p95/p99 and throughput per-gpu. Also capture trace of KV merge step.
Alex: tried local test: forcing fast-causal for mb=4 reduces streaming p99 from ~520ms -> ~340ms but throughput drops ~12% on non-streaming workloads. So it's an explicit latency vs throughput knob.
Mateo: maybe we can adaptively pick kernel per-microbatch based on distribution: if batch contains >=60% streaming requests prefer fast-causal, else grouped-attn. Could add heuristic using request_metadata.streaming=true.
Jordan: that matches routing-policy idea. Also consider splitting microbatch by type (streaming vs completions) before kernel selection — slight extra scheduling overhead but avoids kernel mismatch.
Alex: cost of split: additional micro-sched step + smaller effective batch sizes. For our latency SLO (p99 <=400ms for tier 'interactive') split looks promising.
Sam: other lever: reduce mb_size for streaming endpoint (per-route override) to 1 or 2 while keeping general default 4. That keeps throughput for bulk jobs.
Priya: agree. quick mitigations: per-route mb_size override + kernel-override A/B test. long-term: implement 'batch-aware kernel routing' + KV-merge optimizations.
SREbot: deploy-canary: canary env updated with per-route override feature flag (flag:streaming_mb_override=true) by Sam at 1719001300
Alex: I'll run 4-hour sweep overnight with traffic replay and attach traces in the morning. Thanks for quick thoughts everyone. :pray:
